doc: Semantics a port must reproduce (verified by an independent direct convolution with no scipy: it agrees to 5.8e-8 on every smoothing case): each row is filtered along longitude with its own sigma s = min(w/4, sigma_km / (px_km max(cos lat, 1e-3))) pixels, px_km = 2 pi R / w, only when s > 0.3 (otherwise the row is copied); then every column is filtered with sigma_km / px_km. scipy gaussian_filter1d: kernel taps -r..r with r = int(4 s + 0.5), weights exp(-0.5 x^2 / s^2) normalized to sum 1, accumulated in float64 and rounded to float32 once per pass; mode "wrap" is periodic (indices modulo w, even when r >= w), mode "nearest" repeats the edge row. The smallest grid worth filtering: 2 rows by 4 columns (an impulse in each row), sigma 3000 km on Earth: row sigma 0.42 px (> 0.3, filtered, r = 2), column sigma 0.3 px (r = 1, 2 rows so "nearest" clamps everything). Default tolerance. params.constants lists the module constants and the inline numbers the function reads (a port copies them from its own source and may assert that they equal these).
